mcat_description.short: Tree House is a custom-built or prefabricated elevated wooden structure constructed on or around trees, or supported on stilts, used for eco-tourism accommodation, resort hospitality, children's play areas, and farmhouse leisure spaces. Sold as turnkey construction projects or modular prefab units, primarily quoted per square foot of built area.
mcat_description.long: Tree Houses in the Indian B2B market are elevated habitable or recreational structures built using wood, bamboo, or steel-frame construction, designed to integrate with natural tree canopies or supported on independent stilts. They are supplied as fully custom-designed turnkey projects or as prefabricated modular units that are factory-assembled and site-installed, with design themes ranging from rustic eco-friendly to luxury resort-grade. Primary construction materials include treated pine, teak, bamboo, and engineered timber, with roofing in thatch, PVC sheet, or galvanised steel; all structures require termite treatment, waterproofing, and periodic maintenance for longevity in Indian climatic conditions. The dominant commercial buyers are resort developers, eco-tourism operators, farmhouse owners, and school/park administrators seeking unique experiential spaces.

market_context: Tree houses in the Indian B2B market are primarily supplied as custom-designed turnkey construction projects or prefabricated modular units, with the eco-tourism and resort hospitality segment being the dominant commercial driver — builders operate pan-India across Karnataka, Kerala, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra. Construction materials include treated pine, teak, bamboo, and engineered timber, with support systems ranging from tree-integrated (bolted to living trees with minimal root disturbance) to independent stilt/pillar foundations. Leading Indian prefab wooden structure manufacturers (e.g., Royal Prefab, Vrisa Innovation, FA Thatch Roof, DTH Prefab) offer tree houses as part of a broader portfolio of resort cottages, log cabins, and eco-structures. Timber sourcing increasingly references PEFC/FSC certification as a buyer-facing quality signal. The children's play segment is a secondary but distinct sub-market, with small modular play tree houses sold to schools, parks, and residential complexes. A contamination risk exists from pet furniture listings ('cat tree houses' / cat condos) which share the keyword but are entirely different products — these must be routed to the appropriate furniture/pet products MCAT.
